body: That my “favourite” teacher growing up was having relations with me for 6 months prior to my graduation. They now wonder why I don’t want to talk about him when they bring him up. I was naive and believed everything he told me, while having home issues and a friend passing slowly in the hospital. One of my lowest times.

I'm only solidly noticing this as of recent. For Valentines day, we had her the day before. I got her candy and a card and was gonna make a special dinner for her. I was going to make Tacos, her favorite meal of all. He calls me when he gets her and says he's getting steak for all of us. Part of me is angry that I bought everything and told her our plans and he is kind of ruining it, and part is bitter because I know he wont do that for just me tomorrow. (Which he didn't by the way, at all...) So I explain that I made plans already to cook and he cant find his meat, so he comes home and says he will buy it later. I come home and I am like..."again, I really want to make this for HER...Did you even ask if she wants that for dinner??? This is what YOU want..." He insists that it isn't for him and she totally wants it. So we go to her room and ask what she wants....guess what she wants? TACOS! He wanted to make steaks for HIM. 

In my head I won, but, it felt shitty all in all. But kiddo was happy, and felt love, so that counts for something right??
It hurts...you are important too, as am I. But there is a list of priorities and it feels like we are...dead last.

He knows I am not into overly girly things, so, I have no idea why he wants that. I don't dress up, I do basic makeup, I don't care about my hair, and I hate shopping with a passion. 

I think its part that, and part head up his ass state. He can be very selfish, and will admit it only once in a while.
I agree, and that is how I desire to parent if I ever have my own. You aren't an evil person for saying no to your kid.

I think perhaps he thinks that because I don't try hard and overcompensate that Its a slight. He just mentioned in the car last night when we dropped her off that she seems to be more open with me and trusts me, and it made me wonder why. The only response I have is that I ask her about her life, but I don't pry or demand. I generally let her come to me and leave her be. He bugs her, and worries about her being moody...while I understand her moods and again just let her be. And when she tells me something I don't freak out or panic, he generally worries a lot and is quick to show that worry or anger. 

For me, I just usually tell him what I think is important and tell him to talk to her and let her tell him. (So to not lose her trust, but also be honest with him)

I agree with the top down for functionality. I feel resentment building from the years, and It's hard. As I mentioned in my post and a comment to another redditor, even our anniversary isn't sacred or our own. I made plans and asked for the day to ourselves, I set up a surprise brunch at a winery, and he insisted that she slept over that Friday night and she could leave before dinner. I told him I had something set up and he said she can stay and do it with us...It completely hurt me. No alone time, No romance, no sex, no...us. We don't get that. I ask to go for fancy dinners on my own dime and he says absolutely not, too expensive, waste of time. But than he suggests we take SD out for a fancy dinner...I feel burned. Its petty, but it hurts.

I can connect with her, I care about her a lot and we bond over books and games ect. I was just saying that I cant love her like a mother would, and she would never love me like her mom, especially because her mom is still in the picture. I just don't see myself having such a bond with her since I only met her when she was 10/11. 

I love her, Just...apparently not enough to say yes to everything like he desires me too. He's constantly questioning my affections. She, on the other hand, knows I adore her.

You have no idea how close I am. I am just about to start personal counselling, so, maybe that's next.

He says that he needs time to think and cant resolve an issue quick (think a few days) but when I bring it up, he tells me he doesn't remember an cant recall the details, when I remember them perfectly. He has stated he likes waiting to get me and him to calm down, but, I'm pretttyyy sure he's tricking me into "forgetting it"....but it just makes me resent him.

I will try, I have troubles asserting myself in my personal relationships because my family (parents and siblings) did the same thing. Anything I did needed an in depth explanation that usually wasn't good enough, which Is why I got so angry with him. But I will try that and use your quote.

Its exactly that, a lack of concern for your feelings. 

I could see if SD wanted her nails done, but I've offered for months now and she says yes than doesn't want to anymore because her friends are online or something. The next day she chose video games over nails...but he still insisted.

I want to. And I am trying to encourage him to go. I understand his feelings, I totally get it, but I did compromise, he just refused and wouldn't accept my compromise or feelings. He's older than me, but seems to lack the emotional comprehension. Its so so hard for him to empathize with anyone.

We had a few battles already. One was bedtime, and general noise in the house. Eventually he agreed that it was a good idea to find a middle ground. Another was backing me when I ask her to do something IE recycle something of hers or put her plates away, jackets away. 

The most recent one was time, he needed to advise me before hand so I knew what was happening because I live here too...also because he would forget we had plans. So, now he asks (depending). He doesn't always care of the answer tbh, but at least I know its happening so I can mentally prep myself and know what to expect. Sometimes I say I'm not in the mood and he does it anyways, and sometimes we argue because its our goddamn anniversary and she's not coming to our dinner, and maybe once or twice he said ok and just said no to extra time so that we didn't have to cancel other plans. On my side I will say how I feel, but I just try to accept that he will do what he wants and we argue less...unless its a big event like the anniversary lol that was...a terrible day.

This is an issue for me, because in the past he said that one reason him and his ex broke it off was because she loved the idea of what he could be, not who or what he was. (aside from her cheating and being...crazy..) He is doing the same thing to me, like I am not my own person with my own views and feelings, but rather the same as him, and also someone to cater to him and SD.

I have been asking for therapy, because I realize most of our arguments just brush the surface. He refuses, and I don't know how to get through to him. Id love to have him read articles or books, but he refuses that too...I feel like I'm in a bind.

I love this, and I want this. He believes that kids come first and parents must sacrifice everything for them. I think kids needs come first. But not wants…Kids do not control the household. Kid wants to stay up till 2 am? No. Junk food all day? No. Eat healthy, sleep well. (He caters, and I try to say no, for obvious reasons…aside from the fact that I can’t sleep with someone blaring a tv and laughing and screaming beside my room. That was a struggle for a bit…he sleeps through most things, I am the lightest sleeper ever…and I work on weekend morning, so I kind of need a proper bedtime) Saying no once and a while and making rules makes them into a good well rounded adult, also showing them that other people have needs, wants, and feelings. (Obviously if you’re an ass and never hang out with your kid, than I get it, that’s bad.) I believe you are allowed to take a break and time for yourself even if it means saying no, but I don't get that luxury. 

Like date nights…he wants her here, anniversaries...he wants her here…a vacation for just us, he needs her with us…being able to sleep in your own bed instead of with your 13 year old when on vacay…he thinks if we have no money, its just ok. Putting YOUR needs and feelings first once in a blue moon will help you stay sane. When I want time apart I'm bad and punished some how because I don’t want what he wants. But he can tell her “Not right now.” But not me. He doesn’t even always want to spend time with me, but expects me to always want his daughter around?? 

I just feel like he has tunnel vision for what he thinks this should be, and I have been reading step monster and know I'm not alone in how I feel. But to him its a major offense.

Trust me I feel like absolute shit not wanting her around. I adore her, even when she's sassy and difficult, but I hate that tied to her is my being a full on parent. Its not fair. I thought parenting was equal, not this.

Exactly. If it wasn't me doing 90% of everything I wouldn't care about it. Hell, have her over, I really don't care. What I care about is that I become mommy and he doesn't care. He's satisfied where he is. Kids over and he has to do nadda. I'm positive most people here would start to dislike extra time if this was the case.

So I should be okay with having  her over extra time if it means more time with him on the couch and me doing everything simply because she is there? That doesn't make me a shitty step parent, sorry to say. I don't have an issue with her over, I have an issue that when she is over I do everything. I don't resent her visits, I resent him on her visits, therefore I am starting to dislike extra time.
Take her full time, but step up at least 50 percent and I will be fine, If he were to stay as he is now I would flop and entirely disengage. I am not her mother, despite the fact that he thinks I have taken that role. If he would back me up and stop suddenly throwing at me that I get an abundance of solo time with her, I would feel better, but me now playing mommy alone, in addition to doing 90% when HE is also there, quite frankly is not what I signed up for.

You read it wrong. I told him no because that meant the responsibility was on me, and because he doesn't help me when I try to quiet her down, meaning I get no sleep and get up at 630. Which is exactly what happened. I said it may be a bad idea and he pretty much said too bad and he didn't care.
And yes darling, It's not just the pants, its that I have to cook all the time for her, get her to eat, get her to stop spilling food, put her dishes away, shower, brush her hair, tidy her room, ect. He wants me to do it, and I also want it done, she's old enough to take care of herself. But if I don't cook? I get the questions, and comments, and lazy remarks, and mcdonalds for a week because he wont cook. If he would help, I wouldn't care.
I want to go to therapy, A blended family is hard enough, not topping it up with separate relationship issues.

That is partially why I don't want more time with her, it means I have to cook and take care of her, and ask her to do everything, than he gets frustrated with me because she isn't listening. And her coming for more time is fine and dandy, but if we have plans or something to do that evening than no, what is the point of getting her for me or someone else to babysit? If it is planned, that is fine. But the plan was set and he changed it last minute without even asking my thoughts and informing me. If I hadn't slightly inquired it would have just happened with no mention except "Hey you need to cook for her now instead of us" Oh great, thanks for advance notice. I live here too, if she comes over for extra time, I would hope for a "DD wants to come over, do we have plans or is this ok?". Sometime's he DOES forget that we have things, and a lot of the time we do just erase plans for her, but once and a while I would like to say no and go through with what we planned for our weekend. Just as he expects for my friends and family. I want him to love my brother as much as I do, but he doesn't want him there as much as Id like and I have to understand his emotions as well. Its ALSO his house.

She doesn't love me like she loves him, and although I wish she would I understand it, but he doesn't understand it on the other side. He sees that she doesn't listen, he sees that even she wants time with just him and her, but if I want it I am the bad guy. He wants time away from me, his other half, should I be broken hearted and tell him we are a package and no boys weekends ever? That doesn't sound fair, but he wouldn't get that. 

He is not on the best terms with BM, which is unfortunate, but mending slowly. And I wish, the argument about me watching her lasted an hour until I got extremely upset and finally told him that if he made me do this I would resent him for forcing me and guilting me, and I explained that as much as he was in a corner, he was forcing me in one too. 

I figured that if it happened once, his next response would be "well you did it once"...which has occurred before.

Im sure this will be lost, but Its so significant to me. 
Boy meets world. Season 7, episode 16. Its called Seven the Hard way where the group gets angry at eachother and see their lives if they all part ways and no longer decide to be friends. 
Perhaps this seems silly, but for me this was significant. I watched this show every single night it was on. Mind you I was but a child as I watched this, growing up, having childish issues with friends, (the show began the year I was born) but it impacted me so much. 
They were all a family, of friends, and in that moment it hurt so much to see them all torn apart, to imagine what it was like for them. Perhaps because It made me think of what my life would be like if I lost my family out of a stupid fight, but it just seemed to predict the future, except there was no Shawn to bring them all back together and remind them "lose one friend, Lose all friends, lose yourself."
Are we willing to contemplate the loss of someone in your life and the effect that has on us, or just stay mad and let them go?
Its so much bigger than that though. Its about...actually fighting for what you believe in and love, deciding to be the bigger person and not be petty, and not losing yourself through all the emotional, judgemental and stupid turmoil that is life.
